_README: Human-asserted minutes for players the data cannot model: promoted clubs,
new signings, anyone with no recent Premier League history.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Such a player projects at zero and is invisible to
the optimiser -- preseason that is 203 of 572 players, including ~97% of
Coventry, Hull and Ipswich. But promoted-club players are not worthless:
measured across two cohorts they return 47-100% of an established club's
points per minute, and that spread tracks the team's goals conceded, which
the model already knows from bookmaker odds.
So the model can supply the scoring rate. What it cannot supply is whether
he plays: FPL's own preseason pricing predicts eventual minutes at only
rho 0.175 for these players. There is no data-driven shortcut, so a human
asserts it here. No entry means no projection -- that is deliberate.
HOW TO FILL IT IN. Find candidates with:
python3 scripts/project.py --needs-assumption 3
then add an entry per player you believe starts. Base it on evidence --
predicted lineups, preseason friendlies, a manager's comments -- and put
that evidence in `source`. Then rerun project.py.
id      FPL element id, from --needs-assumption
name    for humans only; `id` is what matches
xmins   expected minutes per gameweek, averaged over rotation and
injury risk. A nailed starter is ~80, a rotation risk ~45,
a bench player ~15
p_start probability he starts (optional; defaults to xmins / 90)
source  the evidence, and when you saw it
Projections built from this file use REPLACEMENT-LEVEL rates -- the median
for that position, scaled by the team's attack rating -- not observed ones.
They carry assumed=1 in projections.csv. Treat them as the weakest numbers
in the file, and revisit once real 2026/27 minutes exist after GW3-4.
Delete entries once a player has real history; the model will then use it.
